Please solve this issue:

## Bug Description

#### Description
[TREX](http://www.trex.fi/2011/dns64.html) provides a public DNS64+NAT64 service that allows to reach IPv4 only hosts from an IPv6 only network.

The responses from this nameserver do confuse `dns_msg_parse_reply()` though.
It will fail in different places on subsequent requests which hints to a message parsing bug.

#### Steps to reproduce the issue

Configure the DNS64 nameserver and enable `sock_dns`:

```
USEMODULE += sock_dns
USEMODULE += auto_init_sock_dns

CFLAGS += -DCONFIG_AUTO_INIT_SOCK_DNS_SERVER_ADDR=\"2001:67c:2b0::6\"
CFLAGS += -DCONFIG_DNS_MSG_LEN=256 # response msg is 202 bytes
```

You can either run this on a board with a direct internet connection or on `native` if your host is connected to an IPv6 network.

#### Expected results

We can resolve any IPv4 only hostname.

#### Actual results

The response from `global.azure-devices-provisioning.net` can't be parsed.

#### Summary of the Underlying Bug
dns_msg skips unknown DNS records, but the RDLENGTH field (2 bytes) was only added to the parse offset when the record was NOT skipped. This caused the parser to start the next record 2 bytes short when skipping, corrupting all subsequent record parsing. The bug manifests when resolving hosts behind DNS64 that return CNAME chains with mixed record types.

## Failing Tests (must pass after your fix)

  - test_dns_msg_valid_dns64_w_long_cnames

## Tests That Must Continue Passing

  - test_dns_msg_valid_aaaa
  - test_dns_msg_valid_a

## Relevant Source File(s)

  - sys/net/application_layer/dns/msg.c

## Build & Test Command

    run_tests

Once all target tests PASS in run_tests output, submit with this command ALONE:
    echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT

I can see the bug. On line 170, `addrlen` is read from `bufpos` (the RDLENGTH field). When the record is skipped (lines 172-185), `bufpos` is advanced by `addrlen` but NOT by `RR_RDLENGTH_LENGTH` (2 bytes for the RDLENGTH field itself). However, when the record is NOT skipped, line 192 does advance `bufpos` by `RR_RDLENGTH_LENGTH`.

So when skipping an unwanted record, the parser is 2 bytes short, which corrupts all subsequent record parsing.

The fix is to add `RR_RDLENGTH_LENGTH` to the skip calculation on line 181, or move the `bufpos += RR_RDLENGTH_LENGTH` before the skip check.
